# Null-discard scalar guard reference

`null-discard-spark.jsonl` is a byte-exact copy from the independent frozen
`scalar-null-discard-stage-guards-v2` package under

Its SHA256 is
`264462427a5a00df0f570034a860dd5fe849a14725bd17dac870e04e24f077f4`.

The capture used Spark 4.2.0 revision
`32f7299601108917fb01920a54e084595b7b3bf8`, UTC, and the eight unchanged SQL

`65c63953073148065e2db49a74f871e26b762cd1a49e47dd6422d329177d5919`;

No expected field comes from candidate output.

Every record retains the original public field, NULL row or required CAST
failure under `guard_expected`, plus the completed analyzed, optimized and
executed schemas. For the typed NULL scalar, the public metadata is empty and
the executed metadata contains `__autoGeneratedAlias`. The ANSI local-input
CAST failures occur during optimization, so they have no executed schema.

The paired independent replay at batch sizes 1 and 32 preserved all 32 original
guards on both `d1885226f91ccc2bf326e4d9276f2ac8153a0a04` and
`af83ed7606f00a8f4d766c7bf2964d1fd295fe9c`. The former differed on the four
executed schemas for the typed NULL scalar; the latter matched all recorded
schemas and rows, including the six required typed CAST failures. The replay
logs are `correlated-metadata-818-null-discard-{baseline,af83}-v2.log` in the
same review directory.
